Slides and video recording of the talk "Analyser lʼétat des données pour mieux les relier" by Cristobal F. Barria Bignotti from the Musée d'Art et d'Histoire Genève, held at the Museum für Kommunikation in Bern on October 15th, 2025 (in French). The talk starts from common obstacles when institutions share data: unclear field meanings, varying degrees of normalization, different vocabularies and date formats, references to external entities and rights. As a collaboration protocol, it presents the Semantic Reference Data Modelling (SRDM) method. The method assesses how usable a dataset is, identifies the preparatory work needed and produces a structured inventory as a first step towards modelling. The slides go through its components: a glossary, a general description of the dataset, and inventories of entities, attributes and data types. They then cover normalization, duplicates, uncertainty and ambiguity, the data lifecycle, and rights and licences. Throughout, examples come from museum collection data.

## Learning outcomes

After working through this resource, users will be able to:

- identify the typical problems that prevent data and datasets from being shared between institutions
- describe the steps of the SRDM method for assessing a dataset
- build a structured inventory of entities and attributes, including data types, normalization status, duplicates, uncertainty and ambiguity
- use the method as a shared protocol to prepare data for modelling and linking
